title: oncall-scratchpad-2026-03-04
body:
On-call notes for 2026-03-04 (shift: 18:00-06:00)

Summary:
- Relatively quiet overall but saw a burst of 5xx errors on hosted-api around 22:12 UTC. Pager triggered twice for high 5xx rate and increased tail latency.
- Root cause immediate hypothesis: backend DB connection exhaustion causing inference-serving timeouts and 502/504s.
- Mitigation: scaled replica pool, cleared stuck connections, enabled circuit-breaker fallback to smaller model variant.

Pager timeline (timestamps UTC):
- 22:11: alert: alerts/high-5xx-rate-hosted-api fired (threshold: 1.5% 5xx over 5m)
  - Incident created: SRE-814 (JIRA)
  - Initial triage: spike correlated with a deploy on dedicated autoscaler (deploy ID: deploy-2026-03-04-21:58). PR link: infra#342
- 22:15: second alert escalated when p95 latency > 1500ms for 2m
- 22:18: identified high DB connection count on inference-main-db (pg-stats: max_conn=500, used=498)
- 22:22: mitigation actions applied:
  - temporarily increased DB connection limit on replica (db-settings-prod) by +50
  - restarted inference-worker pod group 3 to clear stuck clients (k8s rollout restart deployment/inference-worker-g3)
  - enabled fallback routing to 'gptx-small' model variant for write-heavy endpoints (routing rule hash-ff)
- 22:35: alerts resolved; slow decline to baseline over next 10–15m; post-incident monitoring enabled

Actions taken (commands & quick notes):
- kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=inference-worker -o wide  # identified pod restart candidate
- kubectl rollout restart deployment/inference-worker-g3
- psql -h inference-main-db -c "select pid, state, query from pg_stat_activity where state != 'idle';"  # found long-running client connections
- Updated temporary DB limit via terraform var (applied quick patch) -> monitor
- Added a temporary routing rule in the service mesh to prefer smaller model variant on high-latency paths

Immediate follow-ups (TODOs / checkboxes):
- [ ] Finalize root cause: correlate deploy-traffic with connection leakage (assign: Maya)
- [ ] Add metrics on client connection churn to alert earlier (owner: Lucy)
- [ ] Revert temporary DB connection limit change after capacity review (owner: Ethan)
- [ ] Rollback or patch deploy if deploy-2026-03-04-21:58 contains offending change (owner: infra team)
- [ ] Update runbook section on 'DB connection exhaustion' with concrete mitigation steps and commands (owner: Ethan)

Runbook TODOs / improvements (longer term):
- Automate fallback routing when p95 latency > X for 3m (runbook currently manual).
- Add a short-lived connection pooler (pgbouncer) in front of inference-main-db for connection isolation per pod group.
- Create a test that simulates sudden burst of concurrent inference requests and validates connection pooling + circuit breaker behavior.
- Instrument code to track per-request DB client acquisition/release latency and leak detection (traceID correlation).

Open questions / notes to self:
- Why did the deploy cause a connection surge? Possible leaking client or change in connection pooling settings in model server code. Need to check PR diffs for model-serving client init.
- Did autoscaler spin up more pods than DB can handle concurrently? Check HPA events around 22:00–22:10.
- Consider setting a hard cap and queueing at service layer instead of letting pods overwhelm DB.

Customer impact:
- Some customers reported timeouts and 502s for ~20 minutes. No data loss. Legal/CS notified via #customer-impact (message sent 23:05 UTC).

Communication & next steps:
- Draft short postmortem stub in SRE-814 (assigned to me). Include timeline + mitigation notes + TODOs.
- Sync with infra team tomorrow 10:00 PT to decide on revert vs patch.

Quick snippets to copy into postmortem:
- "At 22:11 UTC on 2026-03-04, alerts fired for elevated 5xx errors & increased p95 latency on hosted-api, traced to database connection exhaustion after a deployment (deploy-2026-03-04-21:58). Mitigation included increasing DB connection limit, restarting a subset of inference-worker pods, and enabling model fallback routing; system returned to baseline by 22:50 UTC."

Personal notes / post-shift:
- Remember to run the two queries from the runbook to get historical DB connection charts and attach to JIRA.
- Follow up with Maya on whether the client library update was included in the deploy.
- When writing runbook updates, include exact kubectl/psql commands used above and escalate matrix.

Misc quick logs (to copy into JIRA):
- k8s events around incident: kubectl -n prod get events --sort-by=.lastTimestamp | tail -n 30
- top 5 slow queries during incident from pg_stat_statements snapshot (saved to /tmp/pg-snap-2026-03-04.txt)
summary: On-call shift notes + incident SRE-814 (DB connection exhaustion, temporary mitigations, TODOs)
